body:
## Divyansh policy override: current authority

This supersedes the proposal's earlier format-preserving alternative and design-only outcome restriction. Rui is early development. Implement the simplest correct design with **no backward-compatibility engineering**: no shims, dual readers, legacy preservation or migrations. Store format, outcome strings, wire and fixture layouts may change. Never silently reinterpret old data. Bump actual format/version markers for incompatible meanings; incompatible startup must fail clearly and point to the existing [Start fresh after a Store format change](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui#start-fresh-after-a-store-format-change) recovery path. No user Store reset or relocation is authorized.

L1 now implements output-fact separation from Turn scheduling, not merely its design. Store retains identity/provenance/authentication/atomicity/privacy. The adapter supplies grammar-validated immutable output facts; core policy and the owning transaction decide continuation and Turn outcomes. The chosen target will be reported with each checkpoint; physical provider-specific names will not be retained solely for compatibility. The prior migration alternatives are historical rejected alternatives, not current work or decision requests.

L4 still follows reviewed/qualified L1 in the same isolated worktree as a separately identifiable branch. Renderer reservations and absolute CI priority remain. No landing, main writes, Mac runner, live Store, renderer-file edits or parked-lane resumption. The #531 future old 3239-byte compatibility bound is removed; privacy and no-new-descriptors remain requirements.

Cross-family review is mandatory for READY. A Sol-only adversarial review does not satisfy it. Do not spend renderer's Claude allocation. Spare cross-family capacity is not confirmed and is currently a qualification blocker, while implementation and local checks continue.

Integration dependencies are explicit. L2 owns the atomic ScratchBudget API/caller checkpoint: `reserve`/`reserveUpTo` account only, `allocate`/`allocateUpTo` may reclaim, and `WithoutReclaim` names disappear. L1 supplied an owner-approved two-call Store patch against the pinned base; it preserves automatic eviction and is not independently executable before that API. L3 owns a narrow model_adapter interpretation checkpoint and its ScratchBudget caller migration. L1 waits for its exact published artifact before modifying model_adapter grammar callers. Rejection tags must report output/failure facts, not choose Turn scheduling. No speculative API adoption or compatibility wrappers.

Baseline observations, audit numbering, parked-branch evidence limits and the #530 H2 census defect in the proposal remain valid source observations. Proposed qualification remains required, not passed. No release-blocker closure follows from publication or implementation authority.

<details>
<summary>Earlier architecture proposal and source inventory (superseded where noted above)</summary>

# RELEASE-BLOCKER: provider interpretation and durable Store ownership

## Status and authority

**Release blocker by Divyansh's explicit policy. Architecture proposal with a subsequently authorized format-preserving implementation lane.** Divyansh judges provider grammar inside durable Store not release-ready. Store must enforce identity, provenance and atomic publication over raw immutable provider bytes plus certified projections. Provider adapters own grammar and interpretation. Tool classification is a pure decision invoked inside the transaction. Proposal authentication must survive the separation.

The initial design-only authorization was superseded, before proposal publication, by Divyansh's explicit L1 then L4 implementation direction relayed by Puck. Authorized L1 checkpoints are (a) acyclic output-format/metadata/string-codec leaf, (b) adapter-owned provider/usage/evidence interpretation and pure tool classification, (c) pure compaction-purpose decisions applied inside the transaction. Persisted bytes and Store format must remain unchanged. Stop any incompatible step and publish its one-way-door decision. Persisted outcome/continuation changes remain DESIGN ONLY. L4, only after L1 review and qualification, replaces mutable report-capture failure classification with typed failures while retaining Store lock and validating stored values before encoding. L4 must have a separate branch/checkpoint.

Implementation destination is isolated worktree `/tmp/rui-complect-l1-l4`, base `cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff`, L1 branch `wip/complect-l1-provider-store`, then stacked L4 branch `wip/complect-l4-report-capture`. Renderer has absolute CI priority. No Mac runner, live Store, renderer-reserved file edits, Claude quota, main writes or landing. Hosted mapped Linux/macOS checks and both upgrades are authorized for these changes only, subject to renderer capacity. No nested implementation lane. Catalog #530 and diagnostics #531 remain parked. Publication of off-main reviewed CI-green commits and a morning packet for each lane is authorized, not merge/release.

This issue is the preserved proposal. [CODING_STANDARDS.md, Contract maintenance](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/CODING_STANDARDS.md#contract-maintenance) puts unresolved decisions on GitHub issues and accepted behavior in ARCHITECTURE.md. No parallel ADR or accepted ARCHITECTURE edit is created. If approved, replace the affected owning sections in ARCHITECTURE.md and the evidence cases in VERIFICATION.md through a separately authorized implementation lane.

## Evidence and attribution

Baseline inspected directly: [main cdad5aa](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/commit/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff). Local HEAD and fetched origin/main both matched that revision during inspection. This is source analysis, not execution evidence.

The [actual final audit](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1500e-2a79-72ed-9be6-b9e1b1a69b57), final response message 87, calls the Store/provider dependency cycle **#2** and frontend ownership **#6**. Its compaction-policy finding is #3. Earlier reports used different ordering. The final audit recommends an acyclic shared output-format module for #2 and a pure policy extraction for #3. It does not establish a reproduced corruption bug or declare this issue a release blocker. The broader release policy and target in this issue are Divyansh's decisions. Frontend #6 is outside this lane; the final audit explicitly found no data race under the current join discipline.

### Source observations

| Observation at the baseline | Direct evidence | Design consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider output depends on Store-owned grammar/metadata types, while Store invokes provider validators. | [provider_output.zig:4](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/provider_output.zig#L4), [615–656](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/provider_output.zig#L615-L656); [store.zig:548–560](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L548-L560), [3420–3433](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L3420-L3433). | Moving a parser without removing its dependency on Store does not remove the cycle. |
| Store defines `reasoning=1`, `message=2`, `function_call=3`, `compaction=4`, plus scratch metadata tags and a 104-byte record codec. | [store.zig:733–886](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L733-L886). | Separate adapter grammar, the transient metadata exchange and the durable format. Scratch codec edits alone are not necessarily a Store-format change. |
| Store reads `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens` from saved private JSON and combines them with SQL traversal for compaction. | [store.zig:4915–5085](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L4915-L5085). | Adapter interprets usage. Pure core policy selects purpose from transaction-owned facts. Missing/ambiguous usage must not become zero. |
| Store's accepting transaction recognizes `bash` and `edit`, parses Bash arguments, classifies rejections and creates Actions. | [store.zig:6190–6405](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L6190-L6405). | Descriptor parsing and pure tool classification need separate ownership; the transaction still applies the decision against frozen tools and current permission facts. |
| Durable model evidence has `response_id`, `body_model`, `openai_model`, `x_openai_model`, `request_id`, `usage_content_id`. Item kinds and projection decoding are also persisted meanings. | [model_operation and model_output_item schema](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L7507-L7596), [answer_text_projection](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L7621-L7629). | A neutral-looking rename can still change the Store format or collapse distinct evidence. |
| `continued`, `tool_calls`, `context_overflow` and `interrupted` select runnable work. `continued` also identifies successful compaction together with `purpose=1`. | [selection SQL](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L32-L78), [purpose selection](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L4915-L5003), [acceptance](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L6434-L6498), [partial indexes](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/src/store.zig#L7643-L7647). | These are core scheduling meanings, not disposable provider prose. Move their decision logic without renaming/reinterpreting saved values. |

**Hypotheses, not demonstrated defects:** split ownership makes parser, projection and scheduler changes easier to apply inconsistently; an unchecked caller-supplied certificate could permit reference substitution; a new usage parser could silently change old compaction choices. These are risks the design must prevent, not claims of observed exploits, data loss or extra connections.

## Proposed ownership

Store keeps the durable relation graph, format checks, content integrity, privacy, historical visibility, current Attempt checks, immutable publication, complete tool-group coverage and fencing. The provider adapter validates successful streams/items, identifies consequential variants, interprets usage and served-model evidence, extracts proposal fields and reconstructs compatible replay. Core tool policy decides whether a decoded proposal is executable under the frozen catalog. Core continuation policy decides what may run next from Store facts.

The interfaces are provider-neutral descriptions of validated facts, not a generic provider framework. Use one small acyclic output contract and bounded byte/decoded-string codecs. Provider interpretation imports that contract, not Store. Store may invoke a trusted adapter verifier through that contract, but the verifier receives bounded byte sources and field certificates, never SQLite, Store handles or permission to write canonical state. The existing adapter orchestration may still consume Store's Operation-bound historical view. The pure parser/verifier must not import that orchestration back into Store.

```text
sealed immutable capture -> adapter validation -> bounded candidate/projection stream
                                                       |
                                                       v
Store transaction: binding + byte integrity + certified fields + pure core decisions
                                                       |
                                                       v
                 atomic raw items, projections, calls, Actions and Resolution

historical Store view -> adapter replay validation/encoding -> sealed request
```

### Candidate and projection contract

The candidate carries the producing Operation/Attempt binding, exact source extent and digest, ordered raw item extents/identities, typed core roles, public text/field projection recipes and adapter evidence. It is a bounded cursor over charged sealed scratch, not an item-count-sized in-memory collection. Preserve raw **accepted item bytes and accepted usage evidence**. This does not mean retaining whole HTTP responses, SSE framing, token deltas or rejected/partial bodies as canonical continuation.

For every projection, retain its source-item association, transformation, source range, decoded length and domain-separated decoded-content digest. The four proposal fields remain `item_id`, `name`, `call_id`, `arguments`. A generic bounded JSON-string decoder can implement a certified transformation without knowing Codex field names or tool syntax. Text concatenation keeps ordered parts. An opaque private item remains private even when it backs a public verified projection.

Certification means that trusted adapter validation established a field's relationship to a specific original item. It is not a cryptographic signature, a caller assertion or a new durable `valid=true` flag. SHA-256 identifies bytes; it does not grant authority. Only the trusted adapter selected from the Operation's frozen provider binding constructs candidates. A network request, plugin, report renderer or arbitrary test callback cannot choose a different verifier or assert that an unverified digest is certified.

Store checks source bounds, overflow, complete source reads and digests while importing, even on deduplication. It checks ordered item/call counts and uniqueness, and revalidates the current Attempt after entering the transaction. The candidate and source remain owned/immutable until acceptance and disposal complete. Source mutation, short read, stale binding, import failure or failed commit publishes no partial answer, call or Action. No external network/filesystem fetch or credential acquisition occurs inside the transaction.

### Tool classification stays inside the transaction

Adapter extraction proves which exact raw item supplies each decoded proposal field. The tool module parses the Rui descriptor into bounded facts, including whether arguments are valid, optional description and timeout. The pure decision takes those facts and the **proposing Operation's frozen tool catalog**, not today's Session catalog. Store invokes that decision inside the accepting transaction and applies its typed result.

Preserve today's decision precedence, including disabled Bash reporting `unknown_tool`, enabled Bash with malformed arguments reporting `invalid_arguments`, offered-but-unimplemented Edit reporting `tool_unavailable`, and unknown tool reporting `unknown_tool`. Do not opportunistically enable Edit or change rejected-call discoverability. Labels remain bounded to 100 UTF-8 bytes and never grant execution authority.

Store reads current permission mode/revision inside the same transaction when creating an Action, as it does today. Removing Bash during an in-flight request does not rewrite its frozen offer. Classification alone never starts an effect or authorizes permission. All four references, rejection/Action relation, description certificate, sequence positions and final Resolution publish atomically. Stop, interruption or a replacement Attempt can still supersede the candidate.

### Proposal authentication remains mandatory

Keep one owner check shared by page/cursor/field and exact Action inspection. It verifies Session, producing Operation/Turn, Attempt, item/call ordinal, Action/rejection linkage, canonical item-ID digest and all four public field lengths/digests. Exact reads, execution and replay additionally authenticate the four decoded references against the **original accepted private item** through the trusted adapter verifier.

A second valid Bash descriptor, another public string or deduplicated backing for a different item is not authority for this proposal. Lightweight polling may continue to use admission-certified metadata without reopening payloads. It must not expand that accepted optimization to exact inspection/execution/replay. Missing requested public identity stays an ordinary unavailable result. Contradictory provenance, missing required owners or private/missing exposed fields still fence Store. Unsupported but intact continuation fails the Operation explicitly; it must not be confused with corrupt canonical state.

### Usage and continuation are separate decisions

Adapter usage interpretation returns either a valid pressure anchor or unavailable usage, with source provenance. Keep current rules: a valid total wins; otherwise require the valid unique top-level input/output pair; incomplete/invalid/duplicate split counts are unavailable, nested fields do not count. Preserve the current treatment of each accepted legacy payload, including duplicate totals and integer boundaries, until a separately approved semantic change. Do not improve a parser during extraction and call that behavior-preserving.

Store collects retained-input sizes, complete-result coverage, selected base, historical binding, active-Turn/overflow facts and pending-prefix identity under its existing transaction. A pure core decision combines them with frozen effective compaction policy. Preserve equality at the trigger, reservation arithmetic, overflow-in-active-Turn behavior, unchanged-context failure and the post-compaction successor exemption for the same pending prefix, including failure before projection. No cached pressure model or second frontier is introduced.

Model `resolution_code`, Turn `outcome_code`, `last_failure_code`, purpose, retry eligibility and complete tool results remain distinct facts. A successful accepted model response can mean a completed Turn, continuation for pending input, a tool group, or a compaction result. A failed response can permit compaction or end the Turn. Provider status text cannot decide these transitions directly.

## Store-format decision: A authorized as a constrained implementation, B remains design only

### A. Preserve format 24 and every existing meaning

**Authorized implementation direction, not release clearance.** Move grammar and policy to their owners while a legacy durable codec keeps exact physical schema/encodings. This offers the smallest compatibility risk but leaves legacy provider-named storage fields. That residual is explicit and cannot be waved through the release blocker.

The exact format consequences are:

- Keep `application_id`, `PRAGMA user_version=24`, Store selector, wire version, all tables, columns, SQL constraints and partial-index predicates unchanged.
- Keep item-kind integers 1/2/3/4 with their existing meanings. A codec may map them to typed facts, but cannot reinterpret them as new generic meanings in place.
- Keep the distinct nullable `response_id`, `body_model`, `openai_model`, `x_openai_model`, `request_id`, `usage_content_id`. Adapter evidence access uses neutral typed roles; the legacy codec maps each separately to its old column. Do not coalesce aliases, fabricate missing evidence or replace the requested model with served evidence.
- Keep `model_tool_call.field_metadata` as the same four little-endian u64 lengths plus 32-byte digests: 160 bytes, in the same field order. Keep item-ID digest domain separation, content privacy/deduplication and existing public identity/position behavior.
- Keep `answer_text_projection`'s six columns and existing JSON-string decoding/part-order semantics, including exact source-relative offsets and decoded digests. Moving generic decoding is not permission to normalize JSON or materialize a second answer copy.
- Keep every saved outcome/rejection/failure string and all scheduling/index semantics. A typed codec may centralize them, but no spelling, accepted-set, null/empty distinction or recovery decision changes.
- The 104-byte output metadata exchange is transient scratch, not itself the Store format. Both its producer and consumer must change together; no persisted bytes are inferred from its layout.

There is no migration, backfill, dual write, startup recertification or version bump for a genuinely equivalent extraction. Old-format reads must yield the same answers, actions, retry accounting, compaction base and corruption classification. Merely leaving `schema_version=24` is not evidence of compatibility. If any persisted meaning cannot be preserved, stop this option and request B or a narrower explicit decision. The release blocker remains open until the coordinator accepts the residual legacy encoding and the implementation meets the proof bar.

### B. Replace the physical provider-shaped format

Choose this if provider-specific physical schema is itself part of the release blocker, or if accepted interpretations cannot be mapped losslessly under A. **A new Store format is required.** Use the next unallocated `user_version` at implementation time, not an assumed globally reserved 25. This proposal does not authorize it.

Proposed durable delta, to be finalized as DDL before implementation:

| Existing representation | Proposed replacement and required preservation |
| --- | --- |
| `model_output_item.item_kind` constrained to 1–4 and provider-ID digest | Ordered raw-output owner rows retain Operation, Attempt, Session, position, ordinal, exact private content and opaque identity digest. Core roles distinguish proposal/text/context-anchor associations; Codex's grammar discriminators remain in raw bytes and adapter interpretation. Replace affected item-kind predicates/indexes together. Preserve uniqueness, provider order, group completeness and visibility at acceptance. Do not remap old integers in place. |
| Six provider evidence columns on `model_operation` | An Operation-owned bounded evidence relation separates provider namespace, evidence source/role and exact value or content reference. Preserve response ID, body-reported model, both observed model headers, request correlation and usage bytes as distinct facts, with absence distinct from empty. No generic arbitrary-key bag, unbounded observation log or catalog rows. Update every Current/Full/failure/replay reader explicitly. |
| `answer_text_projection` and four call-field certificate references | A typed projection representation binds a public value to its original raw item, ordered part/range, explicit generic transformation and decoded length/digest. Retain the current four-field certificate guarantee and proposal-owner linkage. Existing deduplicated content remains content identity, not a replacement for proposal provenance. Raw private bytes and projected public bytes must still validate independently. |
| Overloaded string resolutions that imply continuation | Prefer core typed meanings with a one-to-one mapping of existing states; separate provider diagnostic codes from core transition meaning. If new columns separate response result from continuation disposition, define which single record owns each fact and update every selector, index, report and recovery path. Do not keep independent old and new writable authorities. No revised compaction/continuation policy is implicit in this schema work. |

Counts, effective frozen policy, Attempt accounting, original admission keys, input cutoff, selected compaction lineage, complete Tool Result pairing and Action authorization remain canonical. New evidence/projection rows publish with their owning result, not as eventual repair. A stored representation/codec discriminator, if needed, versions byte interpretation only; it does not pin an adapter build or grant new cross-model compatibility. Decide that discriminator's finite values before writing new bytes.

Without the migration framework, existing policy is preserving refusal, **not a successful upgrade**. [ARCHITECTURE.md, Store format and upgrades](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/blob/cdad5aaf4dc43cbb7864f0fa0a4a08bf4f25a8ff/ARCHITECTURE.md#store-format-and-upgrades) and [#523](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/issues/523) require prompt refusal naming both versions and safe options, with no saved-work modification. Users retain a compatible build at the original path, or explicitly approve backup of the stopped Store and a separate fresh Store. Neither reset nor migration is authorized here. Changing the version number alone cannot convert history.

If preserving conversion becomes a release requirement, it needs a separately approved extension to #523. Conversion must run under exclusive Host ownership after an explicitly approved stopped-Store backup. It must authenticate every source item/projection and map evidence, outcomes and unresolved work without launching effects, spending Attempts, rebinding requests or guessing old model defaults. Unknown legacy values must stop conversion, not become completed/failed by fallback. Malformed source history must remain detectable, not be repaired silently. An interrupted conversion must leave the original readable by its compatible build or a fully validated new format, never a mixed usable Store. Define backup/restore, commit/version ordering, disk exhaustion and interrupted-conversion behavior before implementation. Store identity remains path-bound; relocation is a different decision.

### Rejected shortcuts

- Moving Store's enums into a `common` file alone removes an import cycle but leaves usage/tool/continuation decisions mixed with SQL. It does not meet Divyansh's target.
- Making Store accept arbitrary opaque bytes and caller-provided digests removes the grammar but also removes authenticated projection/identity guarantees. It is not acceptable.
- Parsing/classifying everything outside the transaction with copied current state introduces stale permission, pending-input and applicability decisions. Prevalidation may supply immutable facts; Store must read and decide current state under its transaction.
- Rebuilding old certificates with today's parser on startup can reinterpret accepted history and fence previously readable work. It is not an unversioned refactor.
- Saving a second replay JSON blob or a copied lifecycle/continuation state creates competing authority and payload growth. Keep raw accepted items plus derived projections and existing canonical transitions.

## Compatibility and failure invariants

1. Same key and intent recover the original saved command answer; a parser/catalog update cannot rewrite admission. Preserve original selected Message outcomes rather than a successor's answer.
2. Historical requests retain provider/requested model, settings revision, input boundary, effort/output contract and frozen compaction policy. Credentials/endpoints remain late-bound. This design adds no adapter-build pin or exact JSON-spelling promise for rebuilt requests.
3. Raw accepted output stays exact, ordered and private. Adapter replay preserves supported open fields and removes only evidenced non-replayable fields, presently item-level `created_by` for the Codex subset. It does not drop reasoning, switch model/family or fall back to an older base when continuation fails.
4. Missing/corrupt required canonical facts fence; intact but unsupported/incompatible provider material yields explicit continuation failure. Unknown consequential live output rejects the whole candidate without effects. Unknown open fields within accepted supported records remain preserved.
5. Commit publishes raw content, certificates, answer projection, call rejection/Action, Resolution and sequence advancement together. Rollback publishes none. Lost reply after commit recovers the committed result without another effect. Cleanup failure cannot rewrite the result or release unconfirmed resources.
6. New reader/old Store under A must preserve behavior, including old null diagnostics. Old reader/new Store under A must retain all prior scheduling and corruption behavior. Under B, incompatible readers refuse before recovery/dispatch and leave saved bytes untouched. Wire-additive fields separately must fit the unchanged old-client bound.
7. Reopening must not fetch a catalog, require live credentials for saved-result inspection, recontact the provider to certify old content, or reconstruct private state from visible Conversation. Request preparation alone determines demonstrated wire compatibility from complete retained material.
8. Bounded streaming and transaction ownership remain. Use fixed byte windows/cursors and charged scratch, not a per-history/per-call heap collection. Estimate new per-Operation evidence and per-projection metadata before authorizing B; no measured memory or latency improvement is claimed here.

## Interaction with the parked lanes

### #530 catalog

Inspected published [90cfbc57](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/commit/90cfbc57dd27a77fca2c614ffd216201a6e2a756), PR body, its branch ARCHITECTURE section and [correction review](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/pull/530#issuecomment-6252667992). The reported integrated unpublished `10bde402c588be98df705ffdb3e0d74b8557c0b2` is only in its owner's orb/bundle. It was not fetched or inspected, and this proposal makes no claim about its integration or qualification.

Published catalog policy uses an account-confirmed fresh snapshot outside Store for new-Session admission. Store receives absence as transient admission input, checks replay/conflict and ordinary validation first, then rolls back an absent-model rejection without saving the command. Existing bindings and sparse updates do not become catalog-dependent. Keep this separation. The proposed neutral provider interface must not persist catalog availability as entitlement, continuation compatibility or saved failure meaning.

The published Store additionally imports `codex_model_catalog` for report observation and has a `ModelCatalogObserver` callback under its lock. That is an analogous provider-coupling point in the actual published delta. A later combined design should pass provider-neutral owned observation facts, or keep provider JSON presentation outside Store's canonical decision owner, without weakening coherent report capture. This is a design integration concern, not a newly proven runtime bug and not authorization to edit #530. Do not hold a network fetch or credential lease under Store's transaction.

The correction review remains **changes requested** for the H2 census. Published handler registration still occurs only at the first non-catalog request headers, so accepted H2 connections that send no headers disappear from `connections`. The review's counterexample reports two accepted connections, one counted connection and zero catalog requests. This weakens the reuse/connection-bound oracle; it does not prove Rui opens an extra connection. A future catalog qualification must count all accepted connections and reconcile separately identified actual catalog-only connections, including unused/unclassified ones. Grammar extraction neither fixes nor clears this defect.

### #531 HTTP error summary

#531 is an **issue**, not a PR. Inspected the issue/discussion and published [wip/http400-error-body at 8fe950c8](https://github.com/DivyanshGolyan/rui/commit/8fe950c89ff48b21a21036a8a331a7168190ac9d). The reported unpublished `93c777af` exists only in its owner's orb; it was not fetched or inspected.

Its published design parses error shape and redacts outside Store, then supplies bounded failure evidence for Attempt-checked settlement. It keeps HTTP 400 permanent, correlation absent when the provider sends none, no summary for scheduled retries, and no historical body reconstruction. Summary bytes are diagnostics, never a Turn answer, tool input or private continuation. Raw immutable *accepted* provider output in this proposal does not authorize retaining raw HTTP error bodies or weakening redaction.

The branch keeps schema 24 and reuses `resolution_content_id` for terminal/retry-exhaustion diagnostics. Baseline already uses that field for some failure classifications. Readers must discriminate success answer, continuation and failure evidence from owning canonical facts, not merely from a non-null content reference. Under A, preserve those contextual meanings; under B, explicitly map both successful content and diagnostic content without exposing either through the wrong public read or replay path. Printed/truncated diagnostics must never become scheduling authority.

The issue's older status comment mentions a persistent `model_failure` Host-log record and +2 descriptors. The inspected published head instead documents one **optional stderr** line only when a summary exists, closes startup diagnostics at readiness, and has no lane-added persistent-log +2 in `descriptor_capacity.zig`. Do not carry the older arithmetic or logging claim forward as a property of this published head. This does not verify the owner's unpublished version. Catalog's independent worker budget still matters if catalog later lands. Recompute the actual assembled candidate's capacity from its code, not by adding historical issue-comment numbers.

Published source contains old-client reply-budget handling and an upgrade-fixture addition for worst-case failure evidence. Their presence is not a current execution pass. The issue's earlier load-related admission fail-then-pass remains unresolved historical evidence unless a qualified later artifact explicitly resolves it. Its shape-based redaction also expressly does not prevent echoed ordinary prose or short identifiers. No diagnosis/test/cleanup work was resumed in either parked lane.

## Proposed future proof, not work run tonight

Approval of a design is not clearance of the release blocker. At an explicitly authorized implementation candidate:

- Use the maintained subsystem selector and existing Store, model/transport, proposal/activity, canonical-failure, dispatch/compaction and installed-upgrade owners. A shared Store/provider change needs its mapped native checks on both supported platforms and release-required broader checks. Do not reduce them to portable parser tests.
- Exercise a pre-change format-24 Store with completed answers, private reasoning/unknown open fields, mixed accepted/rejected tool calls, unresolved permissions, indeterminate Bash, scheduled model retries, compaction plus its later suffix, overflow, pending input and historical diagnostics. Compare public answers, exact proposal fields, raw item digests, authorization, original keys and next-work decisions before/after under A. Do not demand byte-identical SQLite layout after legitimate runtime writes.
- Use asymmetric counterexamples: replace one valid proposal field by another valid descriptor; corrupt a sibling link while skipping proposal presentation; change frozen vs current tools; add input during acceptance; overflow in active vs terminal Turn; trigger just below/equal; malformed/duplicate split usage plus valid total. Require the relevant wrong implementation to fail the intended assertion.
- Reject late/stale candidates and changed source bytes; inject read/import/commit failure and process crashes before/after atomic publication. Verify no orphan public projection or duplicate effect and preserve cleanup failures. No OS-crash/power-loss guarantee is added.
- Under A, exercise old build/new Store and new build/old Store plus the normal installation path at soft nofile 256. Under B, verify prompt foreground/detached preserving refusal, unchanged saved bytes/membership and reread by a compatible build at the original path. Migration evidence is separate if explicitly approved.
- If combining #530/#531 later, requalify exact assembled wire limits and descriptor ownership; retain the H2 unused-connection counterexample and actual catalog-exclusion control. Do not reuse unpublished or historical runs as current-head passes.
- Check bounded streaming under large private items and growing history, integrity through final byte/EOF, lifecycle yields and aggregate footprint. Avoid a second full payload copy, resident call population or saved replay blob. Report actual measurements rather than promising an optimization.

## Morning decisions

| Decision for Divyansh/coordinator | Recommendation | Consequence of the alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1. Can the release blocker be met by grammar/policy ownership separation with the exact legacy format retained, or must the physical Store schema also become provider-neutral before release? | Start with A only if the coordinator explicitly accepts legacy physical names/encodings as a compatibility codec. Keep the issue blocking until implemented and proven. | Requiring complete physical neutrality selects B, a format break and a larger qualification/upgrade outcome. Merely renaming modules cannot clear it. |
| D2. If B is selected, is preserving refusal/fresh Store acceptable for this release, or is preserving conversion required? | Keep #523's existing refusal/no-migration policy unless Divyansh explicitly changes it. No automatic reset. | Requiring successful upgrade adds migration/backup/interruption design and implementation scope. It cannot be hidden in a refactor or delegated to the installer. |
| D3. How should persisted continuation meanings change, if at all? | Under A, no changes at all. Under B, approve an exhaustive old-to-new state/evidence mapping before DDL or writes. Keep policy unchanged. | Splitting/renaming outcomes can alter scheduling, compaction bases, reports and replay even when SQL types still match. That requires explicit semantic and format approval. |
| D4. How do the parked lanes join this outcome? | Leave them parked. Require a neutral catalog-observation seam in the later integration review; preserve unsaved catalog rejection and #531 diagnostic privacy/non-authority. Reconcile against their then-published artifacts. | Resuming them, accepting redaction risk changes or asserting unpublished integration requires separate direction. #530's census defect remains a qualification blocker, not a grammar task. |
| D5. When may implementation/qualification start, and who clears release? | L1 then L4 are now authorized under the exact restrictions above. Renderer keeps absolute CI/resource priority. Coordinator decides whether qualified artifacts satisfy release policy. | No main write, merge or release follows from lane authorization or issue approval. |

## Work completed and limits

At proposal publication, the actual final audit, pinned main source, published parked branches, #530 correction review, #531 issue/discussion, #523 policy and owning architecture/verification conventions were inspected. No nested thread, reviewer, runtime execution, build, CI job, Mac access, implementation or tracked repository edit had been performed. This issue preserves the complete proposal independently of the orb. The unpublished catalog/diagnostic integrations remain uninspected. All future behavior/test claims above are requirements, not passes. Later implementation checkpoints and actual evidence will be reported separately without rewriting these observations into execution claims.

</details>
